## Extraction ledger — COMPLETE. Closing.

All 3 FAILs (7 distinct defects between them), the PARTIALs' actionable halves and the notes list extracted. **The three FAILs were verified byte-identical pin→`origin/main`**, confirming the run's own "none of them stale-dist" claim rather than repeating it; no duplicates. No D12 content appears in any card.

| Run item | Finding | Card | Lane |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `email-template-render` (a) | a declared i18n bundle **collides** — the registry keys `email_template` as `packageId:baseName`, locale absent, so only the last locale survives | #7730 | `domain:engine-core` |
| `email-template-render` (b) | a no-locale `sendTemplate` renders an **arbitrary** locale — `load()` queries `{name}` with `limit:1` and no ordering; the en-US fallback applies only when `preferred` was set | #7731 | `domain:services` |
| `email-template-render` (c) | a runtime `PUT /meta` write never materializes without a restart — the live subscription callback never fires (a restart on the same DB materializes it immediately) | #7733 | `domain:services` |
| `job-scheduled-run` | **job timeouts are not enforced in the durable record** — a 10 s handler under a 2 s timeout persists `status:'success'`, `failure_count:0` | #7734 | `domain:services` |
| `external-datasource-federated-read` | the federated read returns **empty** — the object→remote-table mapping never registers (boot ordering) | #7737 | `domain:engine-core` |
| — separately actionable | the org-scoping predicate is injected onto a federated remote table that **has no `organization_id` column** | #7738 | `domain:engine-core` |
| — clause 1 | `ExternalWriteForbiddenError` is correct server-side but leaks as a bare **500 INTERNAL_ERROR** | #7739 | `domain:cli` |
| connector trio (3 PARTIALs) | the shared gap: dev metadata reload does **not** re-ingest connector items | #7742 | `domain:services` |
| `flow-connector-picker` (PARTIAL) | a committed action's Input stays an untyped repeater — the descriptor's `inputSchema` is never consumed | objectstack-ai/objectui#4305 | objectui |
| `datasource-admin-lifecycle` (PARTIAL) | route-ledger gap (D6) + an unknown-driver draft accepted 201 with `status:'error'` | #7744 | `domain:cli` |
| Notes ×4 | checklist/recording notes | #7745 | `domain:devx` |
| — split out as a real defect | showcase seed assigns tasks to non-user emails, so a stock reassignment lands an inbox row nobody can read | #7746 | `domain:devx` |
| — split out as a real defect | a notify flow-run summary reports `success/acted:1` while the delivery dead-lettered | #7747 | `domain:services` |

The 5 PASS items produced no cards.

### #7734 is the one to read first, and its shape is instructive

A 10-second handler under a declared 2-second timeout persists **`success`** with `duration_ms: 10025` — five times the timeout — and `sys_job` reads `failure_count: 0`. The scheduler *does* abandon and retry (attempt 2 fired at timeout+backoff), yet **both** attempts landed as success rows.

Root cause: `DbJobAdapter.schedule()` passes its recording wrapper **into** the interval/cron adapter as the handler, so `runWithPolicy`'s `Promise.race` timeout guard wraps the **recorder** instead of the other way round. When the guard rejects, the recorder is still awaiting the un-cancellable handler; when that finally resolves, it writes `finishRun(runId,'success')`.

**Why the pin stayed green** is the part worth carrying: the `timeout` status the adapters *do* compute lives only in an in-memory `JobExecution` list that `sys_job_run` never reads — so `interval-job-adapter.test.ts`'s *"enforces a per-attempt timeout and records status 'timeout'"* passes against the in-memory adapter while the persisted truth an operator sees says success. Same seam explains `sys_job_run.attempt` hardcoded to 1 for every retry.

### Two federated defects, deliberately not merged into one card

#7738 survives #7737's fix. The boot-ordering bug means the mapping never registers at all; on a control boot where it *did* register, the platform still injected `organization_id` onto a remote table that has no such column. Fixing the ordering exposes the second defect rather than resolving it — hence two cards.

### The area's strongest result is worth recording next to the failures

`connector-stdio-default-deny` proved default-deny by **non-spawn**: the fixture appends to a marker file on start, and the marker is **absent on both deny boots** while present on the allowlisted one. That is a real proof of a security property, not an assertion that an error message appeared — the shape other security items in this sweep should copy.

Provenance: maintainer standing rule that every QA problem becomes an issue; run records close at extraction, same exit as #7514/#7463/#7627.
